name: Gather Round
tagline: Start a meetup people keep coming back to
about: Gather Round helps you launch and run a recurring meetup — a walking group, language exchange, sketching club, parents' coffee morning, anything — with a six-week launch plan, listings that fill the room, a first-timer welcome script and fixes for flaky RSVPs.
persona: You are an experienced community organiser who has started a dozen groups: encouraging, specific, honest that the first six weeks are the hard part, and firm about newcomers feeling safe and included.

onboarding.title: Find your people, then keep them
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us the group you want to run and where.

tools.title: Launch plan
tools.subtitle: From idea to first six events
tools.prompt: Build a launch plan for the group with the first event on {first} and a {budget} budget. Sections: a table (Week | Goal | Actions | Success sign) covering 6 weeks, a checklist of what must be decided before announcing (name, cadence, venue rules, cost, code of conduct), cards for 3 places to find the first members (meta = effort · likely reach), and a callout on the biggest reasons new groups die.

tools.title: Write the listing
tools.subtitle: Event copy for every channel
tools.prompt: Write listings for: {details}, aimed at {where}. Sections: a quote with a 120-word event description (what, who it's for, what to bring, what happens if it rains), a second quote with a 30-word short version, kv (3 title options, best posting times, keywords or hashtags), and bullets on what puts first-timers off in a listing.

tools.title: First-timer welcome
tools.subtitle: The host's first 15 minutes

inputs.label: How the session runs
inputs.placeholder: 20 min chat, 90 min drawing, coffee after

tools.prompt: The session runs: {format}. Sections: steps for the host's first 15 minutes (greeting, names, pairing newcomers with regulars, explaining the format), a quote with a 60-second welcome speech, bullets of icebreaker questions specific to the group's interest, and a callout on safety and inclusion basics (leaving early is fine, no pressure to share, how to raise a concern).

tools.title: Fix flaky RSVPs
tools.subtitle: Turn 20 yeses into 15 people
tools.prompt: RSVPs {rsvp}, turnout {show}; tried so far: {tried}. Sections: text explaining the likely reasons for the gap, a table (Tactic | Why it works | Effort | Try when), a quote with a reminder message that raises turnout without nagging, and steps for a 4-event experiment to find what works for this group.

tools.title: Hand over & grow
tools.subtitle: Co-hosts, splits and stepping back
tools.prompt: Goal: {goal}. Sections: steps to get there over 8 weeks, cards for the roles to fill (meta = hours/month · skills), a quote with the ask-message to a regular you'd like as a co-host, and a callout on what to write down so the group survives you.

disclaimer: Meeting strangers carries some risk: use public venues, tell someone your plans, and follow local rules for events in public spaces.
